fieldMarks: Small, fragile-looking lizard, 2-3 in, cream coloured with dark crossbands.
Sexes are not dimorphic in appearance (per CWHR); two forms occur in California: the desert banded gecko and the San Diego banded gecko.
behavior: Nocturnal; peak activity about two hours after sunset, sometimes emerging in late afternoon to warm up; active April-October with a peak in May.
Spends the day under rocks, boards, fallen yucca stems and other litter or in mammal burrows; hibernates in burrows.
Eats beetles, termites, spiders and other arthropods; females lay a clutch of two eggs, buried in soil or under rocks.
habitat: Wide range of desert and semi-arid habitats from creosote and sagebrush desert to pinyon-juniper and chaparral, on rocky areas and sandy flats or dunes; most abundant in sandy flats and washes.
The San Diego form favours coastal scrub and chaparral granite or rocky outcrops.
range: Southern California, southern Nevada, southwestern Utah, western and southern Arizona and extreme southwestern New Mexico, and throughout Baja California and western Sonora; from below sea level to about 2,000 m. Not in Canada.
